- Absence of tobacco use, occupational exposures (silica, beryllium), or infectious symptoms — reduces likelihood of silicosis, berylliosis, or active TB.  
- No history of heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, COPD, or asthma — makes primary cardiac or obstructive pulmonary etiologies unlikely.

[GAPS]  
- Serum ACE level — would support sarcoidosis if elevated (though normal does not exclude it).  
- Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) — needed to exclude latent/reactivated TB, especially given eggshell calcifications.  
- Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) CD4:CD8 ratio — a ratio >3.5 is highly suggestive of sarcoidosis.  
- Transbronchial or surgical lung biopsy — gold standard to confirm non-caseating granulomas and exclude infection (e.g., AFB, fungal organisms) or other granulomatous diseases.  
- Serum calcium — to assess for hypercalcemia, a systemic manifestation of active sarcoidosis.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Sarcoidosis
